title: Theme Engine
subject: ui
summary: How the CSS engine works. The engine compiles a Theme object into a single CSS file that owns all visual styling for the application.

purpose.intro: How the CSS engine works. The engine compiles a Theme object into a single CSS file that owns all visual styling for the application.

snippets.code:
shared/libs/ui/web/theme-engine/
├── conventions.ts     Family prefixes, element→family mapping, selector generation
├── emit.ts            Token-to-CSS emitters (boundary, interior, typography, etc.)
├── theme-process.ts   Main engine: walks theme, generates complete CSS output
├── build.ts           Build script: imports theme, runs engine, writes CSS file
├── index.ts           Barrel export
├── fonts/             Font files (owned by the lib)
├── generated/         Output CSS (one file per theme)
└── sandbox/           Visual test page

claims.text: The only structural knowledge is in `conventions.ts`:
**FAMILY_PREFIXES** — 9 entries mapping family keys to CSS prefixes
**ELEMENT_FAMILIES** — maps each element key to its family
**FAMILY_DEFAULTS** — sensible defaults per family (cursor, transition)
Add an element to the theme → the engine processes it automatically. No registry to update.

reference.statement: The engine has no hardcoded element lists. It walks the theme object dynamically and processes whatever it finds.

claims.text: These exist because tint, smart-bw, and alpha mixing require cross-property composition that plain CSS properties can't express.
**Everything else is plain CSS.** Padding, border-width, radius, shadow, cursor, transition, typography — set directly on cascade selectors. No indirection, no variable chains.

reference.statement: The engine uses **5 CSS custom properties** for composition: `--bg`, `--fg`, `--tint`, `--border-color`, `--bg-alpha`.

claims.text: **@font-face** — font file declarations
**Tailwind variant declarations** — `@custom-variant dark`
**L1: Primitives** — `:root` custom properties (colors, typography, spacing, etc.)
**L1b: Modes + Derivations** — per color scheme (`:root` default, `[data-mode]` others)
**Tailwind token registrations** — `@theme inline` block
**Legacy bridge** — shadcn compat vars (removed as components migrate)
**Base layer** — `@layer base` (body bg/fg, border defaults)
**Property application** — tint/alpha composition on `[element]` and `[layout]`
**Family & element extras** — scrim, placeholder, scrollbar, disabled, icons
**Cascade** — L2 families → L3 elements → L4 concepts → L5 contextual → axes → sizes
**Component overrides** — `[data-slot]` integration (removed as components migrate)

claims.text: The app wears exactly one theme@version, chosen in `configs/theme/index.ts` (`APP_THEME = { theme, version }`); its vite config aliases `@theme` to that version's generated CSS:
Watch mode: `pnpm theme:watch` — rebuilds on theme or engine file changes.

reference.statement: Reads every `themes/<theme>/v<n>/theme.ts`, runs the engine, writes `themes/<theme>/v<n>/generated/<theme>.css` (+ `<theme>-fonts.css`) beside it.

When the engine encounters `smartBleed` on a contextual child, it resolves the parent's padding/radius/border-width by walking the cascade (L2→L3→L4), then emits concrete negative margins and border-radius values on the child's specific selector. No CSS variables, no runtime computation.

reference.topic: What the Engine Does NOT Do

claims.text: No runtime JavaScript in the browser
No Shadow DOM isolation
No PR layout class generation
No runtime linting
No component modifications
